function: no_learning; p. 1: LSTM "predicts both traffic demand and rain attenuation to inform the optimization"; capacity allocation and beam-to-gateway matching use linear optimization and a genetic algorithm.
notes: Title and DOI on p. 1 match the DOI given (published OJCOMS version). Exclusion no_learning: the physical-layer function of the work, feeder-link capacity allocation and beam-to-gateway matching of a multi-beam GEO satellite (satellite resource control), is solved by a closed form (p. 8, Proposition 1) and an adaptive genetic algorithm (p. 10-11), and is compared only with WLB, GA, ACO and branch and bound (p. 13-14); none of these is a trained model. Learning appears only as two LSTM forecasters whose outputs feed the optimizer (p. 2: "These forecasts are then used as inputs to an adaptive genetic algorithm"): per-beam traffic demand (traffic prediction, above the PHY) and per-gateway rain attenuation computed from Meteostat rain rates with ITU-R P.838-3 (p. 6-7). The authors set learned control aside (p. 2: RL approaches "suffer from the exponential growth of state and action spaces"). Alternative readings for the reviewer: if the LSTM forecasting is taken as the learned function, traffic forecasting is above the PHY (above_phy), while the rain LSTM forecasts the feeder-link SNR (p. 12, Figs. 10-11), which could be read as NTN channel prediction (area 2); the forecasters are evaluated only by training and test MSE curves, with no predictor baseline (p. 12).
